claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.

The proposed model combines physics-informed machine learning, microstructure-specific heterogeneity descriptors, first-principles data, CALPHAD data, and limited experimental tensile and fracture data.
Lower-order DFT and CALPHAD simulations can provide phase-distribution and local-chemical-fluctuation descriptors for the model.
Targeted high-fidelity local atomic simulations, such as crack-tip models, can capture toughness-related phenomena needed by the model.
Local phase fractions and interatomic-distance distributions can represent the spatial and chemical heterogeneity of the hierarchical microstructure.
Embedding physics constraints and microstructural information in machine learning can avoid exhaustive full-scale simulations.
Learned relationships between structural heterogeneity and mechanical response can predict elastic response, plastic response, and fracture toughness.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with accuracy comparable to full-fidelity methods.
Predictions of Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness will be within approximately 10–15% of experimental values.
The proposed method will reduce computational time by at least one order of magnitude relative to full-scale CALPHAD or DFT-based methods.
Large-scale first-principles calculations are computationally expensive.
Large-scale CALPHAD calculations are computationally expensive.
Generic machine-learning models without microstructure-specific descriptors are less reliable for toughness.
The model is intended for room-temperature, moderate-strain-rate tensile and fracture testing of samples that retain the reported hierarchical heterostructure.
The model will become unreliable when substantial processing anomalies or phase decomposition move the microstructure outside its training distribution.
The model will become unreliable at temperatures or strain rates outside its calibrated regime.
Accuracy and efficiency gains depend on the quality and representativeness of the training data.
The ability of local descriptors to capture fracture toughness remains unvalidated.
A blinded prospective benchmark will compare model predictions with standardized tensile and fracture measurements on hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 samples.
Prediction errors greater than 15% across multiple blinded sample sets, or systematic toughness discrepancies, will falsify the hypothesis.
